title: Stewed seasoned ground beef, Puerto Rican style

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed seasoned ground beef in Puerto Rican style is a ready‑to‑eat product made from ground beef slowly simmered with classic Puerto Rican spices: adobo, oregano, garlic, onion and a splash of vinegar. The result is a fragrant, mildly spicy dish with a deep flavor that can be used as a base for rice, beans, tacos or served on its own.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puerto Rican cuisine blends Spanish, African and Taíno culinary traditions.
Slow simmering makes the meat exceptionally tender and allows the spices to fully develop.
The traditional adobo sauce used in the recipe contains vinegar, soy sauce and dried oregano.
The dish is often served with rice and beans (arroz con gandules) – a classic Puerto Rican pairing.
Prepared beef can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or frozen for up to 3 months.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground beef provides a high‑quality protein source essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The iron in beef helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels and energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is rich in B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish fits well into low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugars.

items.title: Benefits of spices
items.content: Oregano and garlic have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and adobo paste can raise the salt level; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow pathogenic bacteria such as Salmonella to grow.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Ground beef contains saturated fat; those monitoring cholesterol should consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the stewed beef in the microwave or on a skillet and serve with rice, beans, mashed potatoes, or use as a filling for tacos, burritos and wraps. It also works well added to soups and casseroles to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Before eating, heat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 75 °C.
